lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Carmen, it's Kendra. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hey, yeah, I was waiting for your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sounds good to me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: So-so. Up and down.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're weighing it up, and that's fair.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can probably manage three days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Part of you is already moving, and you want to keep that going.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're open to it. You just want it to fit your real life.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What do you think the next step should be?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After treatment I had no energy at all.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Your body is still recovering, and pushing it feels risky right now.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I mean, if I plan it the night before, I can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You think you can do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're still figuring out what works.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I guess.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you mind if I tell you what some people do?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is your daughter able to help?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walks after dinner going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: That took effort.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walks after dinner. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, not really.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Where could the walks after dinner fit in your day?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I don't know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What feels doable for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 4.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Perfect.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Take care, Carmen. You're doing great.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Blood sugar claim not raised by participant; unverified for this survivor

flags.reason: Coach states walks 'really help bring blood sugar down' without any blood sugar concern raised by Carmen; this is unverified for this survivor and was delivered as information without linking to her goals.
Carmen repeated the rain barrier; coach moved on at 43 without exploring it or problem-solving indoor alternatives.
Carmen voiced strong change talk ('I have to do something... I feel guilty when I skip it'); coach reframed at 41 rather than eliciting more of her own motivation.
After the open question at 49 and Carmen's 'I don't know' at 48, coach gave only a filler 'Mm-hmm' and did not reflect or pursue her answer.

score.summary: Kendra used frequent reflections and autonomy statements, and Carmen moved to a concrete plan of three 10-minute walks with a confidence rating. However, the rain barrier and Carmen's guilt-driven change talk were not explored, and the blood sugar advice was given without grounding in her concerns.
strengths: Line 10 and 12: complex reflections captured Carmen's ambivalence and her wish to keep up with her grandkids.
Line 26 and 54: repeated emphasis on Carmen's choice ('It's completely your call') supported autonomy.
Line 57: accurate summary of the agreed plan, with confirmation from Carmen at line 58.
Line 55: used a 0-10 confidence scale to test the goal's realism.
coaching_tips: Line 29: ask permission and link the walking benefit to Carmen's own goals before giving health claims; avoid unverified blood sugar statements.
Line 42-43: when Carmen repeats the rain barrier, explore it ('What gets in the way on rainy days?') before moving on.
Line 40: reflect her guilt and fear of recurrence as change talk ('You want to protect your health for your family') and ask what else would help.
Line 49-50: follow 'I don't know' with a reflection or open question instead of a filler, to deepen her motivation.
